analysis: Integration of the Flint paged-only defaults PR. Replayed source shows two production changes plus docs and tests. (1) EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.swift (~lines 80-88): for modelType flint, the provider-wide `global` default is no longer consulted. Environment and per-model non-native values still throw flintRequiresNative, and Flint still resolves to .native. This removes a startup failure under the default `balanced` checkpoint setting and does not allow reduced precision to reach Flint. The global is a local operator setting, so no new trust boundary is crossed. (2) EngineV2Factory+BackendPreparation.swift (~lines 180-183, 219-228): for a FlintModel, auto is promoted to explicit paged, so the crash-loop guard and degrade-on-failure fallbacks no longer apply. Any resolution other than paged throws pagedUnavailable. This is fail-closed: Flint can no longer silently serve on the unqualified contiguous path. The trade-off is availability: a crashing paged path is not auto-mitigated for Flint, and the guard is bypassed. That is an operational concern, not a threat-model regression. Docs and tests (FlintPagedOnlyBackendTests, FlintPolicyTests, FlintContextAdmissionTests, the live test) match the code. They add regression coverage for refusal of contiguous and the kill switch, and for global-default relaxation. The live test now relies on production defaults and still asserts kvBackendKind == .paged. T-041 is unaffected: no change to the SSD cache gate, TTL, HMAC lookup tags, DBK3 crypto or salt scoping. Native precision keeps checkpoint format unchanged. There are no changes to attestation, authorization, key handling or the coordinator wire protocol. Residual unverified items: callers of EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve and handling of pagedUnavailable were not supplied (40 replay units omitted), so I cannot confirm that no caller depends on the previous throw or that refusal does not cause provider crash loops. No qualifying finding.
